eval-bot: nightly-eval | 2026-01-28 06:15 UTC
- pset: pset_v51
- metric: factual_recall@0.8
- delta: -5.9% vs baseline
- failing_cases: 41
Link: https://internal.eval/reports/1764123456

harper: saw the alert too. did someone add a persona or filter in v51?

zach: i touched a handful of prompts to 'clarify audience' — trying to reduce generic fluff for certain templates.

mina: can you paste the change, zach?

zach: short diff below:

zach: ```diff
- You are an assistant that answers policy and operations questions neutrally.
+ You are an assistant that answers policy and operations questions for fintech product managers focusing on payments and merchant flow.
```

mina: ah. that reads like an explicit audience clause. likely narrows answers to fintech framing.

drew: sample failing case from report:

drew: ```
input: "How do I document our incident response runbook?"
expected: generic runbook guidance (steps, owners, postmortem cadence)
model_output: "For payments PMs: ensure chargeback timeline and PSP contact list..."
notes: answer is overly payment-specific, misses general guidance
```

harper: confirmed. pset change caused domain drift, hurting coverage for general users.

mina: was there any model variant or quantization change that could amplify this?

zach: no model changes on the canary; only pset edits. so pset is the likely culprit.

harper: options: revert the audience clause (fast), create a split pset for fintech-specific prompts behind a feature flag, or rebaseline if product wants the narrower behavior.

annie-pm: pinged. @annie-pm any preference?

annie-pm: thanks for the heads up. we don't want accidental specialization to leak to general users. revert for now. we can design a controlled experiment for a fintech persona later.

zach: will open a revert PR for the single prompt change.

zach: PR: https://git.internal/psets/pull/512

eng-ci-bot: CI queued for PR 512 — build 7944

mina: while CI runs, we should add a small regression harness: a domain-breadth test set that verifies outputs don't over-privilege a single audience. add it to nightly.

harper: good call. also add a lint that warns on prompt lines containing regex /for .*product managers|for .*fintech/ as a soft warning.

zach: CI passed and deploy bot starting canary to 4%

eng-deploy-bot: Canary deploy triggered for pset_v51-revert at 2026-01-28 07:02 UTC

(35m later)

mina: canary report: factual_recall delta vs baseline = -0.6% on live sample. failing_cases down 41 -> 5.

harper: revert looks good.

annie-pm: thanks team. revert and then let's plan a feature-flagged pset_v51-fintech experiment with clear routing.

zach: merging revert after 24h of canary health. will also land the domain-breadth test and the soft-lint in the same change so we catch future regressions.

mina: follow-ups: 1) add 100-sample breadth check to nightly-eval; alert if any domain's recall drops >3% vs baseline, 2) add soft-lint ticket PROJ-539, 3) document checklist for prompt audience qualifiers and require PM signoff.

drew: adding PROJ-539 now. also adding a tiny test harness to the PR with 50 user-like queries across ops, infra, and product.

eng-ci-bot: new CI run for pset repo with tests included — build 7948 queued

eng-ci-bot: CI passed

eng-deploy-bot: Canary extended to 5% for 24h per revert workflow

mina: i'll draft a short postmortem and drop into #eng-ml/incidents. noting cause = unguarded audience qualifier in prompt text.

harper: nice work catching this quickly. lesson: any audience qualifier is a change to behavior; treat as major.

zach: agreed — apologies for the churn. will follow the new checklist.
